items.title: What defenders need to know about ARTEX, the agentic AI framework threat actors abuse
items.description: The AI-powered penetration testing framework ARTEX has been abused by threat actors like Storm-0940, Storm-3358, Onyx Sleet, Pearl Sleet, Crystal Typhoon, and Salt Typhoon to accelerate their existing workflows related to network reconnaissance, credential attacks, and web application exploitation. The post What defenders need to know about ARTEX, the agentic AI framework threat actors abuse appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

items.title: The risks of device code authentication for AI coding agents
items.description: Lab research shows how device code phishing, a technique that applies to any device-flow client, can extend to AI coding agents, using GitHub Copilot CLI as an illustrative example. The post The risks of device code authentication for AI coding agents appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

items.title: High volume phishing campaign uses Microsoft 365 outage lures to target multiple industry sectors
items.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence observed a high-volume phishing campaign using Microsoft 365 outage-themed lures to target organizations across multiple sectors worldwide. The post High volume phishing campaign uses Microsoft 365 outage lures to target multiple industry sectors appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

items.title: SCKit abuses ScreenConnect to deploy remote access and target technician sessions
items.description: SCKit abuses ScreenConnect to deploy unauthorized remote access and target technicians. Explore the attack chain, mitigations, and Microsoft Defender XDR hunting. The post SCKit abuses ScreenConnect to deploy remote access and target technician sessions appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

items.title: Trained to betray: How post-training supply chain attacks hijack coding agents
items.description: Microsoft Defender Research and the AI Red Team discuss how poisoned datasets and poisoned model checkpoints can trigger remote code execution and other malicious activities. The post Trained to betray: How post-training supply chain attacks hijack coding agents appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

items.title: The global socket: how threat actors are weaponizing GSocket for stealthy C2
items.description: Threat actors are deploying GSocket on compromised Linux servers to keep encrypted remote access after the original vulnerability is patched. Learn how to detect, investigate, and remediate this activity. The post The global socket: how threat actors are weaponizing GSocket for stealthy C2 appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

items.title: Lessons from 59 Linux Kernel Bug Reports
items.description: Microsoft FORGE Lab researchers used codename MDASH to investigate Linux kernel vulnerabilities, resulting in 59 upstream bug reports, 33 assigned CVEs, and 38 merged fixes. The research includes eight demonstrated local root privilege-escalation exploits and examines the challenges of turning AI-generated findings into validated vulnerabilities and upstream fixes. The post Lessons from 59 Linux Kernel Bug Reports appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .
